meta.titre: Passive Voice: changing between active and passive in every tense
meta.sous_theme: Forming the passive, converting both ways, and special cases

source.epreuve_titre: GCE A/L English Language past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A radio announcer in Yaounde says, "The road to the airport has been closed by the police." The announcer puts the road first because the listeners care about the road, not about who closed it. That is the job of the passive voice. Advanced Level papers ask you to turn an active sentence into a passive one, or the reverse, and the main difficulty is to keep the same tense. In this lesson you will learn a method that works for every tense.

items: A transitive verb has an object; an intransitive verb has none.
A past participle is the form used after *have* (written, built, broken, taught, seen).
The verb *be* has the forms am, is, are, was, were, been, being.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### The idea

In an active sentence the subject does the action: *The cook prepares the meal.* In a passive sentence the receiver of the action becomes the subject: *The meal is prepared by the cook.* The passive is formed with the verb *be* in the same tense as the active verb, followed by the past participle of the main verb.

| Tense | Active | Passive |
|---|---|---|
| Present simple | prepares | is / are prepared |
| Past simple | prepared | was / were prepared |
| Present continuous | is preparing | is / are being prepared |
| Past continuous | was preparing | was / were being prepared |
| Present perfect | has prepared | has / have been prepared |
| Past perfect | had prepared | had been prepared |
| Future simple | will prepare | will be prepared |
| Modal | must prepare | must be prepared |
| Infinitive | to prepare | to be prepared |

### Method from active to passive

1. Find the subject, the verb and the object. 2. Make the object the new subject (*him* becomes *he*). 3. Write the correct form of *be* for the tense and add the past participle. 4. Add the old subject after *by* if it is important, changing *he* to *him* and *they* to *them*.

### Method from passive to active

Take the word after *by* as the new subject, change the verb to the active form in the same tense, and make the old subject the object. If there is no agent, a general subject such as *someone* or *people* may be used.

### Points to watch

- Only transitive verbs have a passive. *The accident happened* has no passive.
- The agent with *by* is often omitted when it is unknown, unimportant or obvious: *The shop was robbed last night.*
- With phrasal verbs, the particle stays with the verb: *They called off the meeting* becomes *The meeting was called off.*
- With two objects, either one can become the subject: *The teacher gave the boy a book* becomes *The boy was given a book* or *A book was given to the boy.*

variantes.nom: Active to passive in any tense
variantes.quand_utiliser: When you must rewrite a sentence in the passive
variantes.contenu_markdown: Keep the tense of the active verb in the form of *be*. If the active verb is *is making*, the passive is *is being made*. If it is *has made*, the passive is *has been made*. Never lose the continuous or the perfect part.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for the active form of a sentence that has by + agent
variantes.contenu_markdown: The agent becomes the subject. *Everything was destroyed by the fire* becomes *The fire destroyed everything*. When the agent is a pronoun after *by*, use its subject form: *by them* becomes *they*.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the active sentence is a question or an order or has an indirect object
variantes.contenu_markdown: A question keeps its question form: *Who wrote this letter?* becomes *By whom was this letter written?* An order becomes *should be* or *let ... be*: *Close the door* becomes *The door should be closed* or *Let the door be closed*. With a verb such as *give*, decide which object you want as the subject.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Rewrite in the passive voice.

The villagers have planted five hundred trees along the road.

etapes.action: Identify the subject, verb and object.
etapes.justification: The subject is *the villagers*, the verb group is *have planted* and the object is *five hundred trees*, followed by the place phrase *along the road*.
etapes.resultat_markdown: S: the villagers; V: have planted; O: five hundred trees.

etapes.action: Find the tense of the verb.
etapes.justification: *Have planted* is *have* + past participle, so the tense is the present perfect.

etapes.action: Make the object the new subject.
etapes.justification: The trees are what matters now, and the phrase *along the road* stays with the object.
The present perfect passive is *has / have been* + past participle, and the subject is plural, so *have been planted*.

etapes.action: Add the agent and check the whole sentence.
etapes.justification: The agent *the villagers* follows *by*. The sentence must keep the present perfect meaning and the same information.
etapes.resultat_markdown: *Five hundred trees have been planted along the road by the villagers.*

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Five hundred trees have been planted along the road by the villagers.**

items.erreur_markdown: *The bridge was build by local workers.*
items.pourquoi_faux: After *was*, the main verb must be a past participle, and the past participle of *build* is *built*.
items.correction_markdown: *The bridge was built by local workers.*

items.erreur_markdown: *The mechanic is repairing the car.* becomes *The car is repaired by the mechanic.*
items.pourquoi_faux: The continuous idea is lost; the present continuous passive needs *being*.
items.correction_markdown: *The car is being repaired by the mechanic.*

items.pourquoi_faux: *Happen* is intransitive, so it has no passive.
After *by*, a pronoun must be in the object form.

items.enonce_markdown:
Rewrite in the passive.

(a) The cook prepares the meals.
(b) The thieves stole the motorbike.
(c) We will finish the work tomorrow.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **The meals are prepared by the cook.**
(b) **The motorbike was stolen by the thieves.**
(c) **The work will be finished tomorrow (by us).**

items.enonce_markdown:
Rewrite in the passive.

(a) The students are painting the classroom walls.
(b) The principal has announced the results.
(c) Someone must repair the road before the rains.

(d) Rewrite in the active: *The trophy was presented to the winners by the mayor.*
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **The classroom walls are being painted by the students.**
(b) **The results have been announced by the principal.**
(c) **The road must be repaired before the rains.** (*someone* is omitted)
(d) **The mayor presented the trophy to the winners.**

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Give two passive versions of: *The headmaster gave the best pupil a certificate.*
(b) Rewrite in the passive: *Who painted this picture?*
(c) Rewrite in the passive: *The council has put off market day because of the rain.*
(d) Rewrite in the active: *Everything in the store was destroyed by the flood.*
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **The best pupil was given a certificate by the headmaster.** and **A certificate was given to the best pupil by the headmaster.**
(b) **By whom was this picture painted?**
(c) **Market day has been put off by the council because of the rain.** The particle *off* stays with *put*.
(d) **The flood destroyed everything in the store.**

items_markdown: The passive is formed with *be* in the tense of the active verb, plus the past participle: keep the tense.
Present continuous passive: *is being made*; present perfect passive: *has been made*; modal passive: *must be made*.
To go from passive to active, the agent after *by* becomes the subject and the old subject becomes the object.
Only transitive verbs have a passive; intransitive verbs such as *happen* never do.
Pronouns change: *by him, by them* in the passive, *he, they* as subjects in the active.
A phrasal verb keeps its particle in the passive: *was called off, has been put off*.
